sentences.text: CORAM:
THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ADITYA KUMAR MOHAPATRA  ORDER 10.02.2025 Order No.
This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual /Physical Mode).

2. Present writ petition has been filed by the Petitioner with a prayer for a direction to the Opposite Parties, particularly Opposite Parties No.2 and 7, not to disburse the compensation amount, which has been kept in fixed deposit and which is likely to mature on 27th February, 2025, in favour of the private Opposite Parties.

3. Learned counsel for the Petitioner, at the outset, contended that there exists a dispute among the legal heirs of late Kandarpa Dash, as a result of which, the compensation amount which has been awarded in favour of the Kandarpa Dash under the Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition and Development) Act, 1957 is in dispute.

He further contended that a civil suit is pending among the legal heirs of late Kandarpa Dash and the same has been registered as C.S. No.39 of 2013, which is ) Smt. Padma Dash vs ) Union Of India on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111409467/

sentences.text: pending before the court of learned Civil Judge (Senior Division), Sundargarh.
4. On perusal of the claim under Annexure-2, it appears that all landed property has been included in the plaint schedule.

It further appears that the compensation amount which has been paid against acquisition of the land is also the subject matter of the civil suit and the same has been reflected in the suit schedule appended to C.S. No.39 of 2013.
5. Learned Deputy Solicitor General of India appearing for the Union of India, opposed the prayer made in the writ petition.
He further contended that since the civil suit is pending among the legal heirs of late Kandarpa Dash, this Court should not entertain the present writ application involving purely disputed facts.
He further submitted that when the suit is pending, exercise of the jurisdiction of this Court under Article 226 and 227 of the Constitution of India is barred.

6. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel appearing for the parties and on a careful examination of the background facts of the present case, further keeping in view the nature of the dispute involved in the present writ petition, this Court is of the considered view that the compensation amount, for which the Petitioner has approached this Court, directly or indirectly, a subject matter of the dispute, and that the land for which the compensation amount has been awarded, is a part of the suit schedule property.

7. In such view of the matter, this Court deems it proper to dispose of the writ petition by granting liberty to the Petitioner to approach the learned Civil Judge (Senior Division), Sundargarh by filing an application to safeguard the suit schedule property.
In such eventuality, the learned Civil Judge (Senior Division), Sundargarh shall pass appropriate order in accordance with law after giving opportunity of hearing to the parties.

8. Further, keeping in view the provisions contained under Section 14(6) of the Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition and Development) Act, 1957, the Petitioner is granted liberty to move the appropriate authority, i.e. the Tribunal for redressal of his grievance.

9. With the aforesaid observation and direction, the writ petition is disposed of.
